caption: The drawing depicts a mechanical device consisting of a horizontal wooden base with two large, parallel cylindrical rollers positioned in the center. The rollers are grey with dark shading, suggesting a metallic or heavy material composition, and have ridged surfaces. On either side of the rollers, there are two vertical wooden supports attached to the base, holding the rollers in place. Extending to the right, there is a metal crank handle with a grey grip, connected to one of the rollers for manual rotation. The base is rectangular and brown, with several metal bolts or fasteners visible on its surface. Two long, dark, threaded metal rods with distinctive spiral patterns extend vertically down from the base at each end, securing the device. Smaller rectangular blocks, possibly metal, are affixed to the top of the base at both ends, each held with bolts. The background is plain, off-white with some subtle texture and light brownish stains. There is some handwriting in the bottom right corner, including the words “Herndon Hightower” and some numerical notations.
title: Clothes Wringer
